_meta.purpose: Physical-description grounding map for the Art Studio / Enzo prompt enhancer. Keyed by canonical name; 'aliases' help the grounder match nicknames and bare surnames; 'desc' is the short visual string to inject. Groups expand into the visual descriptions of their member entries at lookup time.
_meta.sources: Locations + council NPCs from wiki text (campaign canon). PCs and most NPCs derived from the actual portrait art in /images/character-art/. Items are hand-curated from their wiki entries. Creatures come from the stat blocks under Venturia/Creatures/ — the campaign-original ones are described from their wiki lore, and the rest are the standard bench that doubles as Car's Masquerade transformation list. Pure visual detail only.
corrections_applied: Noname is an ORC (the old campaign-data export said human).
Noname's missing fiancé is Maruk Grommarg, an ORC (the old export called him 'Marcus').
Retired player characters are removed from this file outright rather than left as dead entries.
_meta.alias_policy: Only specific, identifying aliases — proper-noun-likes, distinctive titles, and obvious nicknames. Bare profession words ('the cleric', 'the wizard') are excluded from PERSON entries because they cause false positives when prompts mention those concepts generically. Creature entries are the exception: their canonical names are the stat-block names ('Guard', 'Performer', 'Fairy'), so a prompt that mentions one casually will ground to the Venturian version of it. That is intentional.

Venturia.desc: Coastal Gothic-Renaissance city rising in stone tiers up the cliffs of Seravalle island; canals threading every level, masked crowds, autumn light, faint sea-fog at the edges.

Vallombrosa.desc: Forbidden fog-drowned estate at the city's edge; grey perpetual mist, half-glimpsed dead manor grounds, unnaturally still — beautiful and wrong.

Venturian Academy of Veiled Arts.desc: Autumn-colored spires rising from the High Quarter; candlelit arched windows that glow even at midday; dreamlike scholarship rendered in stone.

The Ferriers' Confraternity.desc: Ancient waterbound gondola-guild hall reachable only by canal; weathered, secretive, hung with old charts of waterways that don't appear on official maps.

The Amaranth Theater.desc: Vast opera house crowning the High Quarter, visible across the city; gilded thousand-seat hall with supernaturally perfect acoustics; deep red and gold.

The Tidekeeper's Lodge.desc: Weathered salt-stained timber building with green-copper roofing at the end of the longest pier; interior papered floor-to-ceiling with aging navigational charts.

The Mirrorwright's Court.desc: Converted upper-tier warehouse turned maze of silvering workshops; glass, silver, and mercury; dim and close, smelling of metal and secrets.

The Covenant Archive.desc: Windowless building of black stone in the High Quarter; gray-robed archivists, shelves of vellum contracts, an oppressive hush; older than the city.

The Masquers' Sodality.desc: Maskmakers' guildhall in the Market Tiers; walls of masks from painted leather dominos to elaborate sculptural pieces; workshop clutter and fine craft.

The Undertow.desc: Hidden gambling den built into the harbor cliffs, entered by sea-cave at low tide; flickering lantern light over gaming tables; smuggler's-cove damp and shadow.

St. Viro's Respite.desc: Sprawl of connected charity-hospital buildings in the middle Market Tiers, marked with the Abbey's silver-hand symbol; clean, austere, candle-and-incense.

The Burnt Quill.desc: Converted textile mill turned printworks; ink-stained windows, presses clattering dawn to past midnight, the smell of paper and chemicals over the whole block.

The Tiered Gardens.desc: Cascading hillside terraces of cultivated greenery between the Market Tiers and High Quarter; winding paths and stairs, part working farm and part living artwork, autumn foliage.

Liminal House.desc: Rambling centuries-old compound in the lower Market Tiers; buildings grafted together until the architecture loses track of where one ends and the next begins; worn, institutional.

The Salted Cup.desc: Bathhouse complex built over the city's hot springs; steam, warm stone pools, private alcoves; dim, luxurious, conspiratorial.

The Winecradle.desc: Grand tasting house with soaring ceilings and walls of bottles from across the known world; ceremonial, warm-lit, opulent.

The Echoing Court.desc: Circular open plaza with uncanny acoustics, ringed by tiered stone; a public stage-space under autumn light, prone to gathering crowds.

The Penny Shrine.desc: Single cramped room wedged between Harbor District warehouses, layered with centuries of coins, candles, found offerings, and scrawled prayers; humble, cluttered, devotional.

The Vellum Hall.desc: Converted merchant hall turned public library; good natural light, sturdy shelving of practical books; plain and well-kept.

The Fog Wardens' Garrison.desc: Small stone watch-building and tower at the Overlook, where the city ends and the Vallombrosa fog begins; spare, cold, lonely.

The High Quarter.desc: Venturia's upper city: autumn-coloured towers and polished pale stone above the rest of the island, private salons behind expensive doors, Academy robes on clean-swept streets, wrought-iron lamps and cypress in stone planters; quiet in a political rather than peaceful way, with the whole city laid out below.

The Harbor District.desc: Venturia's lower city at the waterline: working docks, rope and salt and stacked cargo, warehouse fronts, ferry houses and tide-marked steps, sailors' shrines in wall niches, gulls and bell-noise, gondolas going silent under low bridges. Grey-green water, weathered timber, wet stone.

The Market Tiers.desc: Venturia's working middle: terraced lanes and stepped streets of shopfronts, guild halls, taverns, care houses and maskmakers' workshops stacked up the hillside; awnings, hanging trade signs, laundry lines, crowds who all know each other's business. Warm lamplight, ochre plaster, autumn leaves in the gutters.

The Overlook.desc: The cliff-edge district where Venturia's streets stop and Vallombrosa's fog begins: stone terraces and a low balustrade at the drop, watchfires and Fog Warden signal lamps, offerings and tied ribbons left on the rail, grey flat light and a wall of still mist filling the whole view. People lower their voices here.

The Veiled Tower.desc: VAVA's divination tower: a slender autumn-stone spire hung floor to ceiling with veiled and unveiled mirrors, star-charts and scrying basins on brass stands, candle-light doubling wrongly in the glass. Some of the reflections are showing the past.

The Binding Hall.desc: VAVA's hall of contract magic and oath-craft: a severe vaulted chamber of dark wood and pale stone, long witness benches, a raised signing table, wax and seal-matrices laid out in rows, and walls of ribboned contracts whose ink glows faintly where a promise is still holding.

The Glamour Courts.desc: VAVA's illusion training spaces: open colonnaded courts with mirrored walls, costume racks and mask stands at the edges, chalk performance rings on the floor, and half-finished illusions hanging in the air — a face, a doorway, a second sun — none of them quite agreeing with each other.

The Hall of Reflected Faces.desc: The Veil Court's private gallery: a long dim mirrored room holding one mask from every Autumn Masquerade for nearly three hundred years, mounted in ranked gold-and-glass cases and lit by candle sconces; hundreds of empty white and gilded faces looking back from both walls at once.

Sconce Row.desc: A narrow quiet street of tall thin houses over shopfronts, three streets downhill from the Tiered Gardens' lower gate; iron wall-sconces along the plaster, and one house with its shopfront shuttered and boarded for years, two dark rooms above it. Nobody has opened it in a long time.

The Second Bell.desc: The low-ceilinged tavern fifty feet downhill from the Overlook stair, where off-shift Fog Wardens drink: smoke-darkened beams, a long bench along the fog-facing wall that the regulars leave empty, a brass bell over the bar rung only for the second round, rooms upstairs, and grey light in the windows.

The Sorcerer of the Spirits.desc: Lotan's winery and tasting room in the Winecradle: a stone press floor, a short cool cellar of barrels, a worn tasting counter, and living quarters off the back; a rack of coins from a dozen different ports nailed along a ceiling beam. No frontage on the canal side, which suits its owner.

The Prompt Loft.desc: A disused low loft over the Amaranth Theater's north scene dock, reached by two flights of external iron ladder to a shuttered window: crates of retired prompt-books, painted scene stock nobody has needed in years, thick dust, and a view across the theater roofline to the canal.

The Cask & Cube.desc: The real-world room the campaign is played in: a deep-blue wainscoted den under a cedar-beamed coffered ceiling, an oval blue-felt gaming table with leather captain's chairs on a patterned rug, a stone fireplace with candelabra, a lit bottle cabinet, a dartboard in a built-in wood surround, and a wrought-iron lantern chandelier over the table. Warm low lamplight, night in the windows.

Lotan.desc: Tiefling man (he/him), late 30s–40s; red skin; chunky, broad-shouldered build; large curved dark ram horns sweeping back from his temples, black hair pulled back, salt-and-pepper beard, pointed ears; loose white shirt under a brown leather jerkin; easy roguish grin. A pirate's bearing.

Caravel \"Car\" Asteri.desc: Satyr, 19; androgynous and slightly feminine-leaning; pale/fair skin; curled chestnut-auburn hair, curving ram horns, pointed ears, fine delicate features; slim build; dark high-collared coat; almost always holding or wearing an ornate mask, amid a maskmaker's workshop.

Noname.desc: Orc woman (she/her), 24; green skin; athletic, powerful build; small lower tusks, strong features, dark hair drawn back in braids; dark layered leather Fog Warden's coat and armor; guarded and intense.

Valentro.desc: Elf man (he/him), 19; fair/pale skin; thin, lean build; unmistakably pale platinum-blonde shoulder-length hair, tousled and light-catching, with light stubble, blue eyes, pointed ears; a weathered green cloak over leather, bow and quiver across his back; a faint arcane mark on the back of one hand; warm and quiet.

Roxanya \"Roxy\".desc: Adult forest gnome woman (she/her), 19 but with the mature adult features of a gnome: defined cheekbones, a slightly prominent nose, a strong jawline, faint laugh lines at the eyes, not a round childlike face. Sun-tanned skin weathered from outdoor life, scattered freckles across the nose and cheeks. Wild curly copper-red hair pulled into twin buns with loose strands escaping. Sharp green eyes with a knowing, wry expression — a sly half-smile or mischievous smirk, never wide-eyed innocence. Pointed ears. About 3 feet tall with adult gnome proportions: compact but mature build, confident grounded stance — unmistakably an adult gnome, not a human child. Layered brown leather swashbuckler's garb with feathers, well-worn and lived-in. A taxidermy owl perched on her arm.

Lord-Admiral Teodor Vast.desc: Human man, late 50s; commanding, weathered features, silver-streaked black hair; fine fleet-owner's clothes worn with an affected sailor's plainness.

Constanza Marea.desc: Human woman, early 40s; sharp, composed merchant-aristocrat of the Harbor District; elegantly dressed, poised and watchful.

Master Artisan Celeste Orion.desc: Human woman, mid-50s; calloused hands and ink-stained fingers; practical guild-master's dress; sturdy and no-nonsense.

Guildmaster Vincenzo Copper.desc: Dwarf man, middle-aged by dwarf standards; elaborate beard jewelry; rich, conservative metals-guild attire; stout and dignified.

Mother-Abbot Lucia Virosdottir.desc: Human woman, early 70s; slight frame but commanding presence; abbey vestments bearing the silver-hand symbol; austere and devout.

Father Domenico of the Four Winds.desc: Human man, late 30s; weather-worn and restless; the bearing of a former ship's chaplain, in plain travel-priest's garb.

Vincen Tidecaller.desc: Human man, 60s; a permanent horizon-squint; weathered, plain Tidekeeper's clothing; quiet and watchful.

Captain-Commander Thora Ironmark.desc: Half-orc woman, 40s; scarred and imposing; a decorated Watch uniform; direct, hard-standing, soldierly.

Primo Navigante Old Maren.desc: Human woman of uncertain age — sixty or eighty, the canal light hides it; deliberate and unreadable; weathered ferrier's dress; eerily still.

Archmagister Dorian Silvermarch.desc: High-elf man appearing middle-aged by elven standards (near two centuries old); refined VAVA academic robes; brilliant, warm, faintly weary.

Aurelio Volante.desc: Tall olive-skinned man, fifties; easy confident posture, slightly theatrical; well-traveled merchant's dress with a collector's air, a fine mask often near at hand.

Celina Cross.desc: Human woman, ~23; striking, with dark wavy upswept hair and a jeweled silver mask pushed up onto her brow; a deep-blue and silver embroidered low-necked gown, jewels at ear and throat; lit by warm stage light. Magnetic.

Maruk Grommarg.desc: Orc man; dark grey-green skin, a heavy muscular build, prominent lower tusks, a scar across the face, short dark hair, pointed ears; worn dark leather Fog Warden's armor with a shoulder pauldron; grim and steadfast.

Garl Glittergold.desc: Gnome deity, resplendent in gold; a round genial face and broad golden beard, a tall jeweled crown and ornate gold robes; a gem-cutter's hands wreathed in floating multicolored gemstones. Warm, sly, radiant.

Isabella Fortunata.desc: Human woman, young; soft auburn hair pinned up, fair and luminous; a pale ethereal gown of lace and tulle; haloed in warm golden light against a dreamlike ballroom-garden. A tragic-romance figure.

Lorenzo di Errante.desc: Fey-touched man; pale greenish skin, dark hair swept back, sharp features with a single prominent lower fang, pointed ears; a dark high-collared doublet; a candlelit manor behind him. Lean and haunted — drawn as kin to Marcello, the resemblance deliberate.

Marcello di Errante.desc: Fey-touched nobleman; pale grey-green skin, long dark swept-back hair, pointed ears, handsome aristocratic features; ornate dark-and-crimson noble attire; an opulent candlelit interior. Composed and lordly — visually mirrors Lorenzo.

Tolomeo Lucente.desc: Human man, 40s; dark hair, dark beard, weathered; a deep-red explorer's doublet over leather, a satchel and map-case; holding a brass navigational instrument among charts and instruments. A scholar-adventurer.

High Oracle Ysmena Starweaver.desc: Ageless elf woman; pale lavender-tinged skin, pale near-white eyes, long dark hair, pointed ears; a midnight-blue veil and a star-spangled gown, a silver circlet; haloed by drifting constellations. Cryptic and otherworldly.

Cosimo Verdigris.desc: Human man, 70s; silver-white hair and a full beard; dark green and black embroidered guild robes; at work among mirrors in a candlelit workshop. Distinguished and guarded.

Isidore Verdigris.desc: Human man, 40s; dark hair, a neat dark beard, sharp handsome features; a dark green-black craftsman's doublet; handling an ornate copper-framed mirror amid a mirror-workshop. Ambitious and restless.

Thalia Verdigris.desc: Human woman, 20s; dark hair pinned up with jewels, warm tan skin, a bright smile; an emerald-and-gold gown with mirror-shard jewelry; amid chandelier-lit society. Charming and polished.

Silas.desc: Human man, 40s — the same dark hair, dark beard, and weathered features as Tolomeo Lucente, but his face and body are mapped with old scars and burns and brand-like prisoner markings. The comatose stranger at St. Viro's.

The Keeper of Faces.desc: An imprisoned Archfey of masks with no single true face — a tall figure built of overlapping, shifting masks over a blank pale visage; autumn-and-bone palette, glamour like candlelight on water.

Tartuzi.desc: A great volcanic sphinx — a woman's face, a lion's body, broad wings — her hide cracked basalt and cooling stone, soot and ash all over her, lava-like veins glowing through cuts that run across her whole body, set in a volcanic chamber. Present day: she looks defeated and exhausted, her fires guttered low, ashen and dimmed — fused into her prison for a thousand years.

aliases: Tartuzi the Lock in her prime
Tartuzi (in her prime).desc: A great volcanic sphinx — a woman's face, a lion's body, broad wings — her hide cracked basalt, soot and ash like a mantle, lava-like veins blazing bright through the cuts across her body. Regal, powerful, fearsome and unbroken — depicted in her prime, before the imprisonment.

Brownie.desc: A small fey creature, approximately 5 inches tall, with disheveled spiked dark brown hair and striking attractive features. The face is clearly that of a mature adult — weathered with defined features, a set jawline, and the lived-in character of someone well into adulthood, with no youthful or childlike qualities whatsoever. Shirtless, wearing a deer-hide loin cloth and boots, with a rabbit-fur cape draped across the shoulders. Dull red and blue body paint marks the arms. The brownie stands in front of a small cave dwelling carved into a rocky mountainside, with a modest porch. Feathers are woven into the hair and clothing. The setting is a wooded, mountainous region with natural light filtering through the trees.

aliases: the leader of the Veil Court
Valeria Tessere.desc: Human woman, apparent late 30s but plainly older than her face admits; warm olive-tan skin, dark hair braided and pinned up with loose strands at the temple, dark level eyes, an unreadable expression; a deep midnight-blue silk-and-velvet gown heavily embroidered in gold filigree, a jewelled gold coronet and a sapphire collar; holds an ornate filigree gold half-mask on a slim staff, raised to hide one side of her face. Candlelit gallery of hanging white-and-gold masks behind her. Regal and theatrical.

aliases: the way of the leaf mentor
Strider.desc: Half-elf-looking man of indeterminate age, lean and weather-browned with a gardener's hands; dark curly shoulder-length hair pushed back, faintly pointed ears, freckled sun-worn skin, a quiet measuring gaze; a long moss-green hooded cloak embroidered with leaf-work over an undyed linen shirt with rolled sleeves and a leather work-belt; heavy pruning shears hanging at the hip. Usually against birch trunks on the terraces of the Tiered Gardens at dusk, the lamplit city below. Watchful and unhurried.

Professor Emiliana Sarto.desc: Human woman, late 40s; olive skin, dark greying hair escaping a hasty pinned-up knot, ink on her fingers, tired bright eyes behind reading lenses; unfashionable, hard-worn VAVA academic robes in faded russet with chalk dust at the cuffs; carries an overfull satchel of fog-boundary notes, sketch-maps, and pressed specimens. Dogged and slightly obsessive.

Velonar Kaligor.desc: Historical figure, some seven generations before Lotan — a tiefling warlock in his prime; deep red skin, curved dark horns, black hair, a hard-lined face; battered travelling leathers and a patched dark mantle from a decade of campaigning; purple-black otherworldly flame runs up both forearms and wreathes his hands. Depict him in the smoke and ruin of Castle Ravenloft or in the amber-veined dark of the Amber Temple. Exhausted, victorious, and holding a power that is not the one he asked for.

aliases: the druid of the Fifth Order
Andrea Kaliskiny.desc: Historical figure, ancestor of Lotan — a human druid of the Fifth Order of Celtans, 30s; pale skin weathered by travel, long dark-blonde hair in a thick braid with green thread worked through it, steady grey eyes; layered grey-green woollen robes and a hide mantle, amber beads and bone charms at the throat, a rowan staff; Barovian mist and dark firs behind her. Calm, capable, holding knowledge no one else in the room has.

aliases: the bruxa of the Amber Temple
Lady Noctyrix.desc: A bruxa — a vampire the equal of Strahd, dead a thousand years by Lotan's reckoning. A tall, beautiful, imperious woman with bloodless white skin that takes daylight without harm, black hair coiled high, black-red eyes and a mouth that hides its fangs until it does not; a severe high-collared gown of black and old wine-red with amber at the throat. A hall of black marble veined with amber behind her, mad wine-drunk followers at the edges. Beautiful, hateful, unafraid.

Fated One.desc: Campaign-original celestiale (Angelo subtype): the half-remembered shape of a person made of pale starlight — a Medium translucent humanoid with no fixed face, hovering a foot off the ground, robe and hair trailing away into vapour; faint constellations turn inside its chest and cold blue-white light collects at its hands. A soul that should have become undead and became this instead. Sad, weightless, watchful.

Hidden One.desc: Campaign-original celestiale (Angelo subtype) in beast shape: a large four-legged creature of banked white-gold light, lion- and stag-like but of no nameable species, its face blank and eyeless, its outline soft as if seen through gauze; warmth glows between its ribs and its paws leave brief prints of light. Silent, protective, patient.

Radiant One.desc: Campaign-original celestiale (Angelo subtype) as an armoured retributor: a Medium winged figure in plain burnished plate, the helm's face-opening filled with white light instead of a face; hard-edged wings of pure radiance, a greatsword whose edge burns white. Often passing as a guard, soldier, or crusader among mortals. Stern, blinding, judicial.

Arcobaleno.desc: Campaign-original fey — the rainbow fairy: a Small-to-Medium fey with thin iridescent dragonfly wings and a soft prismatic sheen over fair skin, hair and ragged layered clothing dyed in the one colour of the spectrum it has chosen; glittering fairy dust hangs in the air wherever it has flown and a small rainbow arcs behind it. Coastlines, tide-flats, and the light after rain. Loud, warm, hopeful.

Vivo.desc: Campaign-original fey — the bright fairy: a Small quick trickster with luminous freckle-like motes scattered across sea-pale skin, oversized dark curious eyes, cropped bright hair, and ragged sea-glass-green clothes; gauzy wings, and usually half-hidden inside one of its own flickering minor illusions. Can shrink to Tiny or swell to Medium at will. Coastal glades, harbour rafters, ships' rigging.

Il Rosso.desc: Campaign-original devil — the crimson fiend: a Medium humanoid devil the colour of banked coals, its cracked red-black hide glowing furnace-orange in the seams; hairless, with short blunt horns and two ember eyes, heat-shimmer around it and scorch prints where it stands. Can collapse into a man-shaped column of pure elemental fire that pours through keyholes.

Il Caduto.desc: Campaign-original demon — the fallen: in true form a Large hunched shapechanger with charred cracked hide, over-long arms built for leaping and climbing, hooked fiendish claws, and fire visible in its throat and joints beneath a burning-eyed skull-like face; in disguise, an unremarkable Small or Medium humanoid whose expression never quite moves. The reveal is usually the last thing a mortal sees.

L'anima Vuota.desc: Campaign-original demon — the hollow skin: a fiend indistinguishable from an ordinary person, flesh and eyes and mannerisms all correct, betrayed only by something slack behind the face, as though the skin were worn rather than lived in. Plain, forgettable city clothes; a poisoned dagger kept out of sight. Reads as whatever creature type it wishes when anyone looks.

Red Hand of Mammon.desc: Campaign-original devil — a servant of Mammon: a Medium stooped figure in a threadbare merchant's coat, both hands crimson to the wrist as if dipped in hot wax, fingers too long and always counting; gold-flecked eyes, a starved covetous face, coins and gems and stolen trinkets stuffed into every pocket and seam. Greed given a body.

Callus.desc: Pirate duellist and crew leader, CR 7: a lean fast human man in the prime of his thirties, well-kept studded leather under a salt-faded captain's coat, a rapier worn high on the hip and a pouch of crushed glass and ash at the belt; dark hair tied back, a duellist's balance, a scar or two kept as decoration. Unhurried and theatrical right up until he moves.

Torek.desc: Callus's bosun and enforcer: a heavy-shouldered human man in a chain shirt over sailcloth, scarred knuckles, a flattened nose, close-cropped hair; a scimitar in one hand and a belaying pin in the other. Keeps the crew in line with fear and the occasional cracked skull.

Pirate Deckhand.desc: Common pirate crew: a leather jerkin over sun-bleached slops, bare feet, tar-black hands, a cutlass and a handaxe, a crude tattoo or a knotted headscarf. Never alone — they fight shoulder to shoulder.

Pirate Sharpshooter.desc: Pirate marksman: lean and quiet in dark oiled leathers, perched in the rigging or on a crosstree with a light crossbow braced against the shoulder and a dagger in the boot; weather-squinted, unhurried, steady-handed at any range.

Empyrean Iota.desc: A Tiny celestial — a god's stray thought given shape: a hovering mote of divine light the size of a fist, haloed in slow-turning gold script and thin rings, casting light on everything it passes and moving through walls as though they were water.

Giant Eagle.desc: A Large celestial eagle with a fifteen-foot wingspan, bronze-and-white plumage with a faint gold sheen at the feather edges, a great hooked beak and knowing, uncannily intelligent eyes.

Giant Owl.desc: A Large celestial owl, soft grey-white barred plumage, a broad pale facial disc and huge dark eyes; utterly silent in flight, with the still attention of something that understands speech.

Sphinx of Wonder.desc: A Tiny celestial sphinx the size of a housecat: a small lion's body with feathered wings and a soft cat-like face, its dark fur shot through with drifting star-fields and nebula colour, faintly luminous at the edges. Available as a familiar.

Blink Dog.desc: A Medium fey hound with tawny-gold coat, upright ears and pale intelligent eyes; edges blurred and doubled where it phases in and out of the ethereal, leaving brief afterimages when it moves.

Bugbear Warrior.desc: A Large fey goblinoid, seven feet of long-limbed muscle under coarse red-brown fur, a wedge-shaped snouted face with small yellow eyes and jutting lower teeth; scavenged hide and plate, a heavy morningstar, and a silence that shouldn't be possible at that size.

Bullywug Warrior.desc: A Medium fey frog-folk: mottled olive and swamp-brown amphibian skin, a wide lipless mouth and bulging side-set eyes, webbed hands and feet; scraps of looted armour, a rusted spear, and a permanent slick of marsh water.

Dryad.desc: A Medium fey nature-spirit shaped like a beautiful woman grown out of a tree: bark-textured skin in birch silver or oak brown, hair of living leaves and small branches turning autumn colours, eyes like sap-lit amber; steps into and out of trunks as though through a doorway.

Faerie Dragon.desc: A Tiny fey dragon the size of a cat, scales in one saturated jewel colour, butterfly-like membranous wings patterned with eyespots, a long curling tail and a face fixed in permanent mischief; usually caught mid-turn while turning invisible.

Fairy.desc: A Small fey the height of a child, delicate and sharp-featured with pointed ears and insect-thin iridescent wings; clothes cut from petals, cobweb and stolen cloth; leaves a faint trail of light in flight.

Goblin Minion.desc: A Small fey goblin, scrawny and knock-kneed, sallow green skin, oversized flat ears, a snub nose and too many small teeth; filthy rags, a cracked leather cap, a stolen knife. Fragile, and never alone.

Goblin Warrior.desc: A Small fey goblin fighter: wiry green-skinned body, broad flat ears, yellow eyes, a wide mouth of small teeth; mismatched scavenged leather and a scimitar or shortbow, crouched low and already looking for the next place to be.

Hobgoblin Warrior.desc: A Medium fey goblinoid soldier: orange-red skin, a blunt flat-nosed face with dark bristling hair and small tusks; disciplined matched half-plate in the unit's colours, longsword and shield, standing in formation and unimpressed.

Pixie.desc: A Tiny fey barely a foot tall, luminous pale skin, wide dark eyes and translucent moth-like wings that scatter glowing dust; usually only half-visible, laughing, and holding a spell it should not be trusted with.

Quickling.desc: A Small fey shrunken and hollowed by speed: grey-white leathery skin drawn tight over a gaunt frame, sunken black eyes, a needle-toothed grin; permanently blurred with motion — three afterimages for every real limb — and a pair of tiny wicked daggers.

Satyr.desc: A Medium fey with a human upper body and the shaggy legs and cloven hooves of a goat, curling ram's horns, pointed ears and a broad reckless grin; a shortbow or a set of pipes, a wineskin, and no shirt worth mentioning.

Sprite.desc: A Tiny fey the size of a hand, sharp-featured and stern, dragonfly wings and leaf-cut armour, carrying a shortbow of thorn and grass whose arrows carry sleep-poison. Invisible far more often than not.

Worg.desc: A Large fey wolf, black or slate-grey coarse fur, a heavy blunt skull, orange-red eyes and a mouth built for tearing; broad enough to be ridden, and clever enough to resent it.

Abyssal Wretch.desc: A Medium demon barely holding a shape: grey slumped flesh, a lipless mouth and a face rubbed almost featureless, arms too long, hands ending in blunt claws; the failed remnant of a soul, shuffling and mindless.

Dretch.desc: A Small demon, squat and bloated with pallid grey-blue skin, a wide fanged mouth, stubby arms and clawed hands, tiny black eyes; wreathed in its own stinking gas. Stupid, cowardly, foul.

Gnoll Warrior.desc: A Medium fiend with the head of a hyena on a hunched seven-foot frame, matted spotted fur, a laughing muzzle full of teeth, hands ending in black claws; strapped scavenged armour, a notched spear, and blood already on it.

Imp.desc: A Tiny devil, crimson-scaled and knee-high, bat wings, a barbed whipping tail, small curved horns and a narrow malicious grin; hovers at shoulder height where it can whisper, and turns invisible the moment it is inconvenient.

Larva.desc: A Medium soul-slug of the Hells: a pale grub-like body of grey wet flesh, and pushing up out of it the recognisable, silently screaming face of the damned person it used to be. Slow, pitiful, horrible.

Lemure.desc: A Medium devil of the lowest order: a half-melted blob of moulded flesh in a vague humanoid shape, a drooping weeping face with no eyes worth the name, pushing itself forward in a slick of its own substance. Reforms unless holy water gets to it.

Manes.desc: A Small demon drone: a wretched, claw-handed, blank-faced thing of grey rotting flesh with rows of small teeth and black pit eyes; dissolves into a thin sulphurous vapour when killed.

Maw Demon.desc: A Medium demon that is essentially a walking mouth: a hunched legged body dominated by an enormous circular jaw of jagged teeth split down its whole front, tiny useless arms, no eyes. Hunger with a gait.

Nupperibo.desc: A Medium devil, blind and bloated, its face a lipless ring of teeth and its eyes sealed over with grey skin; wreathed in a crawling cloud of biting insects that shows the shape of it. Moves in shoals.

Quasit.desc: A Tiny demon, dark green-black and gaunt, bat wings, spindly clawed limbs, curved horns and a needle-toothed sneer; shifts between this form, a bat, a centipede, and a toad, and is never quite where it was.

Vargouille.desc: A Tiny fiend that is a severed human head flying on two leathery bat wings sprouted where its ears were; green-grey skin, a mouth of long needle teeth, wet writhing tendrils for hair, and eyes that still look like they belonged to somebody.

Acolyte.desc: A junior temple servant of Venturia: plain undyed robes with a rope cincture and the silver-hand token of St. Viro's or a Four Winds pendant at the throat; a censer or prayer book to hand, and the careful over-earnestness of someone still learning the words.

Apprentice.desc: A VAVA student mage: a short autumn-russet Academy robe over ordinary clothes, ink-stained fingers, a borrowed wand and an overloaded book-strap; young, underslept, and trying very hard to look composed.

Bandit.desc: A road or canal-side robber: patched leathers, a hood or a rag mask pulled up, a scimitar and a light crossbow, boots that have outrun somebody. Opportunistic and jumpy.

Commoner.desc: An ordinary Venturian: plain wool and linen in muted autumn colours, an apron or a carry-basket, wooden clogs worn down by the tiers' stairs, and a cheap plain mask pushed up on the forehead the way everyone in this city keeps one.

Cultist.desc: A robed devotee of something not on the Council's list: a dark hooded robe over street clothes, a symbol stitched at the breast, a ritual dagger, and a blank mask with no expression cut into it.

Drow Warrior.desc: A Medium humanoid dark elf: obsidian-dark skin, stark white hair, pale red-violet eyes, sharp fine features and pointed ears; close-fitting dark chain and a spider-motif cloak, hand crossbow and short sword.

Duergar.desc: A Medium grey dwarf: ashen bald head and a wiry iron-grey beard, hard colourless eyes, a body squat and over-muscled from the deep places; plain blackened plate and a war pick. Grim and joyless.

Grimlock.desc: A Medium humanoid gone blind underground: grey warty hide, a flat face with smooth skin sealed over where the eyes were, wide flared nostrils and a jaw of pointed teeth; ragged hides and a stone-headed club.

Guard.desc: A Venturian City Watch soldier: a chain shirt under a slate-and-autumn-gold tabard, a plain half-helm, spear and shield, a lantern hook at the belt; posted at a bridge-head, a gate, or the foot of a tier stair.

Jackalwere.desc: A shapechanger caught mid-turn: an ordinary-looking person whose face is sliding into a jackal's narrow muzzle, ears rising into points and eyes going flat amber-yellow; sand-coloured fur breaking through the skin at the jaw and forearms.

Kenku.desc: A Medium crow-folk: glossy black feathers over a lean humanoid frame, a heavy dark beak, bright inquisitive eyes, stubby flightless wings folded at the arms; layered scavenged clothing full of pockets, and a stolen shortsword.

Lizardfolk Warrior.desc: A Medium reptilian humanoid: green-grey scaled hide, a blunt crocodilian snout, a heavy tail and clawed feet, flat unreadable eyes; bone-and-hide armour, a spiked shield, and a bone-tipped spear.

Orc Warrior.desc: A Medium orc fighter: grey-green skin over heavy muscle, jutting lower tusks, a low heavy brow and dark hair in braids or a scalp-lock; layered hide and scavenged plate, a greataxe held one-handed while shouting.

Performer.desc: A Venturian entertainer: a bright motley of theatre-cast silks and mismatched velvets, ribbons at the sleeve, a decorated commedia half-mask pushed up or held on a stick; a lute, a tambourine, or juggling knives, working a Market Tiers crowd.

Sahuagin.desc: A Medium sea devil: green-black scaled hide fading to a pale belly, a shark's head with black eyes and rows of needle teeth, webbed clawed hands and a finned crest down the spine; a coral trident and a net, dripping harbour water.

Scout.desc: A ranging tracker: mottled green-brown travelling leathers and a hooded cloak, a longbow and a hand axe, boots caked in fog-country mud; quiet, watchful, and dressed to be missed.

Soldier.desc: A professional man-at-arms: matched chain and plate over a padded gambeson, a kettle helm, a spear or longsword and a shield with a house or garrison device; drilled posture and a hundred-yard patience.

Spy.desc: An agent dressed to be forgettable: good but unremarkable city clothes in dark colours, a hooded half-cloak, a hand crossbow and a thin blade both out of sight, a plain unadorned mask in a pocket. Nothing about them stays in the memory.

Thug.desc: Hired muscle from the Harbor District: a heavy leather coat over a barrel chest, scarred knuckles, a broken nose, a mace or a length of chain; stands too close on purpose.

Tribal Warrior.desc: A warrior from outside the city's walls: hide and fur armour, painted markings on the face and arms, braided hair strung with bone and bead, a heavy spear and a hide shield.

Kaligor.desc: Rare magic scimitar carried by Lotan; a slightly curved darkened-steel blade whose edge catches light like the rim of an ember; crossguard shaped as two unfurling flames; KALIGOR engraved along the ricasso; old leather grip rewrapped more than once; its flame is controlled, low, ember-gold, and heirloom-worn rather than wild.

The Listener's Coin.desc: A worn bronze listening coin currently carried by Roxanya "Roxy" and formerly owned by Aurelio Volante. The coin is smooth from long handling, its faces too weathered to read, with subtle magic that lets its holder hear clearly through a solid wall, door, floor, or window for ten minutes before recharging at dawn.

members: Father Domenico of the Four Winds

_notes.tartuzi_two_states: Tartuzi has two keyed entries. Bare 'Tartuzi' grounds to the present-day defeated look; reference 'Tartuzi (in her prime)' (or aliases like 'ancient Tartuzi') in the prompt to ground the regal historical look. The grounder matches by name, so you choose the state by what you type.
_notes.silas_echo: Silas is intentionally built to share Tolomeo Lucente's face, scarred and burned. The 'The Tolomeo Echo' group exists so prompts about their resemblance pull both descriptions at once.
_notes.groups_expansion: Group entries are matched by their name/aliases like any other entry, but at injection time the grounder expands them into the concatenated descriptions of their members. 'Draw the party in the Salted Cup' pulls all 7 PC descriptions plus the bathhouse setting in one go.
_notes.creatures_section: The 'creatures' section is loaded exactly like npcs/items by the grounder (chatbot/vos/services/descriptions.py, _flatten_descriptions). The first thirteen entries are campaign-original stat blocks; the rest are the standard bench, which is also Car's Masquerade form list — so 'Car as a quickling' grounds both Car and the quickling in one prompt.
